Docs/Domain randomization

Domain randomization

Explore appearance and workspace variation without confusing a modified training environment with the fixed evaluation scenes.

Opt in to each variation

RandomizedTableSceneBuilder ↗ supports table appearance, background and lighting variation, with optional table-height changes. Defaults are inert. This procedural builder is distinct from the fixed native-kitchen scene track and does not automatically produce an official benchmark result.

Follow docs/howto_randomize_scene.md ↗ for integration and docs/howto_scene_library.md ↗ for authored interiors. Record which axes are enabled, their ranges, asset sources and seeds. Make one change at a time before combining variations.

Integrate the builder in a task

from tasks.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder

# Inside a task's _load_scene(self, options):
self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder(
    env=self,
    random_table_texture=True,
    random_background=True,
    random_lighting=True,
)
self.table_scene.build()

This fragment belongs in a task implementation; it is not a top-level executable script. Preserve the task's existing initialization and actor placement. If you enable table-height jitter, apply the builder's per-environment table_top_offsets to every table-supported actor; the builder does not move task-added objects for you.

Preserve camera and collision semantics

Randomized appearances matter only when the policy receives images. Keep resolution, intrinsics, sensor order and preprocessing consistent with training. Camera pose randomization is a separate opt-in operation described by the guide; do not shift cameras accidentally while changing a background texture.

The procedural background enclosure is visual and has no collision shapes. It must not be advertised as a physical obstacle. Conversely, native scene surfaces have their own geometry and collision semantics. See Cross-scene evaluation for that separate contract.

Revalidate changed task builds

After editing a task, rerun the functional tests and inspect representative resets and policy-camera frames. Changes to physical parameters, object placement or success predicates can invalidate existing demonstration compatibility. Use the restoration, replay and label-parity checks before reusing data.

Do not alter integrity certificates to silence drift. A record-neutral fingerprint lineage must be supported by evidence, not declared merely because the task still looks similar. Keep randomized-training ablations separate from the published fixed protocol and document them with the reproduction record.
